Careful habits for the upbeat month
This section sets out the plain rules

Companion Animal Travel Desk - Daily Handling and Travel Support
This section sets out how the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps animal travel calm, safe, and steady from check-in to handoff.

We greet travelers in a warm, plain-spoken way and keep the focus on comfort, clarity, and humane handling. Carriers stay upright, secure, and easy to inspect, and every move should be smooth enough to avoid crowding or sudden noise. The ground team handles transfers with care, and staff should watch for signs that a pet needs a slower pace, a quieter spot, or a brief pause before the next step. When a traveler arrives with a pet, we confirm the travel plan, review the carrier setup, and make sure the animal is fit to continue before the booking moves forward.

The desk also keeps close track of lounge use, and <<FACT F006>>. If a traveler asks about a connecting service, staff should stay calm, give a simple answer, and avoid promising anything that has not been checked. In busy periods, we guide people toward the next available touchpoint, keep paperwork neat, and pass along any welfare concern without delay. The pet lounge and the skyport holding areas are to be treated as clean, quiet spaces, and all handlers should protect them from unnecessary foot traffic.

For capacity planning, <<FACT F008>>. Staff should not stack carriers, leave animals unattended, or place one pet too close to another if that would raise stress. Any animal that seems ill, overheated, frightened, or unfit for travel must be reported at once, and the desk will follow the standard hold-and-escalate path before release. If a traveler needs help understanding the process, explain it in plain language and keep the tone reassuring.

For any exception, welfare concern, or routing issue, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
